title: End Exercise — Clock Strikes Noon

fields.resolution: ENDEX. The clock hits 12:00. The AODB server goes silent. FIDS displays across the terminal go dark. Gate management systems show 'NO DATA.' A file appears on the server desktop: 'You should have hired me. — D'. The threat has executed. The airport's flight operations are now disrupted.
finalState: The logic bomb has been activated.
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. Put down your phones and radios. We will now begin the hot wash.
fields.hotWashMethod: 3-Up, 3-Down: three things that went well, three things that broke
hotWashQuestions: What indicators were most critical in identifying the threat?
Why did the SIEM not alert on the scheduled task or service account?
How did the prioritization of physical and cyber actions affect the outcome?
What would have changed if the team had discovered the task earlier?
How should the airport improve off-boarding procedures for contractors?

instructorNote: This is the final inject. All roles have received their cues. The debrief should focus on delayed triage, the failure of routine checks to catch the threat, and the importance of service account hygiene. Collect all documentation and evaluator sheets.
